items.title: fix(agents): sessions_send into a busy session is reported queued but…
items.summary: fix(agents): sessions_send into a busy session is reported queued but never runs (#167126) * fix(agents): sessions_send into a busy session is reported queued but never runs A Gateway `agent` run into a session whose turn is still running was rejected during admission with SESSION_WORK_START_CHANGED: the running turn's own restart-recovery fence made claimMainSessionRecoveryOwner return `invalidated`. sessions_send reported `accepted`/`queued`, the pending input went straight to `interrupted`, and asynchronous reply-backs and failure notices into a busy requester were lost. chat.send into the same busy session queues correctly. When the claim fails only because every fence belongs to a run of this session that is still executing in the current lifecycle (it holds its runtime handle or run context; it may hold its own delivery claim), the command now waits for that run, bounded by its own timeout and abort signal, then prepares and claims again under the unchanged rules. Recovery and delivery debt of any other run, other generations, retained fences without a live execution (for example after sessions_yield), the subagent settle/announce terminal guard and stale-generation rejection keep failing as before. Refs https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/144594 * fix(agents): keep FIFO order and worker-owned reads while admission waits for a live run Review follow-up for the busy-session admission wait. - FIFO: a command that waits for a live run no longer releases its serialized command admission (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/166597). It keeps that admission until it settles and takes the renewed admission nested under it, so later commands for the session stay queued behind it even when its re-preparation is slower. Recovery-owner waits still release admitted work as before. - Storage: the live-run fence check and the wait read the session row through readSessionEntryReadOnlyInWorker instead of the synchronous accessor. Wait notifications coalesce into one in-flight read. A row that is already unfenced when the asynchronous read returns is claimed again once. - Tests move to agent-command-recovery-owner.live-run.test.ts and add two waiters with a delayed re-preparation of the earlier one, plus a check that the wait performs no synchronous session reads. Refs https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/144594 * test(agents): satisfy mock-export ratchet and type-argument lint in live-run admission tests The live-run admission tests do not create recovery targets, so they use the real recovery owner release module instead of a partial mock factory. Refs https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/144594 * test(agents): synchronize live-run admission tests on deferred events instead of polling The FIFO and worker-read cases now wait on the worker read starts and on the earlier waiter's second preparation through deferreds, without real-time polling. Refs https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/144594 * refactor(agents): derive reply recovery promise type from its owner * test(agents): prove reply waits through the native admission fixture Use the existing host-process recovery suite and Vitest context-aware cases. Preserve the existing storeless command admission scope while testing real reply ownership. --------- Co-authored-by: Peter Steinberger Co-authored-by: Holger Gruenhagen

items.summary: fix(ios): keep voice replies and locally held answers in place, and fold injected CLI context (#165473) Fixes: spoken replies could disappear or borrow a consult model label, held answers moved below later history, and injected context overwhelmed native chat. Keep these repairs in shared transcript reconciliation, grouping and notice owners. Preserve full notice payloads in expansion and export. Verified exact candidate 1da5bf54995833e5a8d939d0c912f19ef789bb9c with independent source review, Linux changed checks and green CI. Colin supplied 67 passing shared-kit tests, two passing iPhone UI tests, intended baseline-control failures, lint/format results and inspected native captures. Raw xcresults remain on the Mac; spoken VoiceOver, real Gateway and physical devices are not claimed. Original implementation by Marvinthebored; maintainer integration and validation coordinated with Colin. Co-authored-by: Solvely-Colin Co-authored-by: Marvinthebored

items.title: perf(auth-profiles): offload peer settlement and catalog reads (#166183)
items.summary: perf(auth-profiles): offload peer settlement and catalog reads (#166183) * perf(auth-profiles): offload peer settlement and personal catalog reads * perf(auth-profiles): reuse existing peer database admission * fix(auth-profiles): settle captured peers after uncertain fencing * perf(auth-profiles): reuse admitted schema facts for paired reads * test(gateway): preserve fixture owners and verify oversized history * perf(auth-profiles): set reader busy policy during native open * test(gateway): complete persistent fixture cleanup ownership * fix(auth): admit replaced OAuth peer databases Retire a retained validation receipt for a different physical file before a new native opener captures its publication guard. The new worker still performs its normal admission, and revocation after capture still refuses publication. The physical-replacement refresh regression failed five times on the PR and passed five times on main. Existing integrity and reclamation suites pass after the repair; no SQL, schema, or public API changes are added. * perf(trajectory): reuse admitted maintenance readers Read retention aggregates through the existing maintenance lane so stale sweep retries do not repeatedly open and admit snapshot helpers. Keep the full read outside the canonical writer reservation, with captured physical identity and current authority checks. Retain the writer begin/delete operations, lease fences, retry bound, retention policy, and scaled inspection budget. Remove the superseded helper operation and extend the existing append-during-read and cleanup coverage. * perf(sessions): reuse admitted maintenance revision facts * perf(state): reuse cold reader schema admission facts * test(gateway): preserve store selection during fixture reset * test(auth-profiles): drain fixture workers before peer repair * test(state): align retained-reader SQL budgets * perf(sqlite): combine catalog admission metadata reads Read catalog objects and the published user version in one pinned compound query. Keep a separate version row for empty catalogs, the native fallback for operator objects that shadow the table-valued PRAGMA, and the post-catalog freshness probe that refuses peer upgrades before data reads. Use a compound SELECT to avoid a SQLite 3.53.4 native column-metadata crash observed with the joined form. The former query crashed in five full-file runs while the prior implementation passed all five; the compound form passes five full 45-case runs and all 121 tests in the five owner suites. New metadata budget regressions fail with the former two-read implementation. Fresh P2 review is clean. The exported declaration surface is unchanged from the completed SDK report. Strict full-workload remeasurement remains a pre-publication gate; no prior failed samples or phase windows are excluded. * perf(gateway): skip unchanged mention snapshot transactions Keep changed Inbox snapshots atomic, but return after the existing head read when its revision is unchanged. Retain the initial snapshot path and reread changed heads inside the transaction before loading sources. Restore separate native schema metadata reads after the combined-query optimization exposed SQLite crashes on Linux. Preserve cold freshness, authorizer, rollback, and upgrade checks.
